source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / ASPIRE Project, IFAD-funded - "ដំណាំក្រូចថ្លុង" (Pomelo Cultivation Guide), 2017, 90pp
text:
Citrus stink bug (ស្រ្តីងបែតង, Rhynchocoris poseidon, also recorded as Rhynchocoris humeralis, family Pentatomidae) feeds by piercing young fruit and shoots and sucking sap, which causes fruit to drop prematurely or develop hard, discolored, poor-quality patches where feeding occurred. Both nymphs and adults feed this way, and damage is most serious on young, developing fruit.

The bug develops through several nymphal stages before reaching the winged adult stage, and populations can build up over a growing season if not managed, particularly where nearby host plants provide it shelter between citrus fruiting cycles.

Because stink bugs are relatively large, slow-moving, and visible, and because they tend to aggregate, hand-collection is a practical control option in smallholder orchards, in combination with monitoring during the fruit-set period when damage does the most economic harm, and targeted insecticide use where populations are heavy.
